description: A torn sheet of web, still sticky at the anchor threads. Nothing in this valley admits to spinning it.
lore: Six gold, the cheapest thing in the trade, and it sells steadily all year. Ask a dealer who buys web and he will tell you: people with doors. A thread pulled across a doorway at shin height, stuck down on the tacky ends, tells you in the morning whether anything came through in the night.

There is a man at a lapsed fire out on the western grass who strings one every evening. It has never been broken. He is not checking for what comes in: he has been [[lore/the_quiet|Faded]] two years, he knows the order these things go in, and what he needs to know each morning is whether he went out — whether a shape stood up in the night and walked a round of the yard wearing his hands. He has begun setting a second thread at the back door, having worked out that a man in that condition would use the door he always used, and it was never the front.
gm_notes: The cheapest junk in the game buys a man a daily verdict on his own thinning. He is right about the back door, which is the part that should land after the reader has moved on.
